structuredIncident.summary: The R3 exit carrier beam fell from the yoke into the mill pit at approximately 1:03 PM on October 14, 2024 (Turn 2). The incident occurred during an outage preparation phase where work rolls and backup rolls had been removed. Specifically, the top backup roll balance was left isolated in a raised position, and B hydraulics were shut off and bled. Two contractor employees witnessed the fall; no personnel were in the pit at the time of impact.
structuredIncident.focalEvent: R3 exit carrier beam falls from yoke into mill pit
structuredIncident.actualImpact: Falling object (SIFp) with potential for death; equipment damage to sled and scaffold platform observed. No injuries reported as no team members were in the pit.
structuredIncident.potentialImpact: Severe injury or fatality if personnel had been present in the mill pit at the time of failure.
structuredIncident.normalState: Carrier beam installed on yoke with keeper; B hydraulics pressurized (implied by 'shut off and bled' action); Top backup roll balance supported/contained. Work rolls and top/bottom backup rolls typically installed during normal operation, but removed for outage work in this case.
structuredIncident.eventState: Work rolls and top/bottom backup rolls removed; Top backup roll balance isolated and raised; B hydraulics de-energized (bled); Carrier beam fell intact with keeper still on link. Small window liner also dropped from operator side.

evidenceClaims.text: The R3 exit carrier beam fell from the yoke into the mill pit at approximately 1:03 PM on October 14, 2024.
Work rolls and top/bottom backup rolls had been removed prior to the incident.
The top backup roll balance was left isolated in a raised position.
B hydraulics were shut off and bled prior to the incident.
The carrier beam fell intact with the keeper still on link.
No personnel were in the mill pit at the time of impact.
Two contractor employees witnessed the fall.
B hydraulic system was shut off and bled for work on that system. Pressure removal may alter support or restraint.
The 'isolated' state of the top backup roll balance may have shifted load paths to rely solely on hydraulic pressure or mechanical retention that was compromised by bleeding.
The carrier beam fell intact with its keeper still installed on the link, indicating a failure of retention under specific load conditions rather than simple disengagement.
The 'isolated' state of the top backup roll balance may have altered load paths or removed a critical support point for the yoke/carrier beam assembly.
The 'isolated' state defined by workers (raised balance, bled hydraulics) may have altered load paths or support points for the yoke/carrier beam in a way not covered by standard equipment tags.
Carrier beam fell intact with keeper installed, suggesting failure of load retention or support rather than mechanical fracture under normal operating loads observed at impact.
The specific mechanical design of how the carrier beam interacts with the yoke when hydraulics are bled and balances are raised is unknown, representing a gap in current evidence.
Missing mechanical assembly drawing (EV-004) prevents verification of load paths and keeper engagement under the specific failure conditions.

The incident description notes 'B hydraulics were shut off and bled' but does not confirm if a functional test was done. Failure to verify zero energy before leaving equipment in an unstable configuration is a common LOTO gap.
Mechanical assembly drawing (EV-004) prevents verification of load paths and keeper engagement under specific failure conditions.
Missing mechanical drawings (EV-004) prevents confirmation that the equipment was configured according to design intent or safety standards.
The specific mechanical design of how the carrier beam interacts with the yoke when hydraulics are bled and balances are raised is unknown.

answerFetches.answer: Evidence indicates that de-energizing (bleeding) B hydraulics likely removed hydraulic support, but evidence does not confirm if this was a 'critical restraint' sufficient to prevent the fall on its own. The carrier beam fell intact with the keeper installed while the top backup roll balance remained isolated in a raised position.

nodes.label: Carrier Beam Falls Intact with Keeper Installed
nodes.detail: The R3 exit carrier beam fell from the yoke into the mill pit at 1:03 PM. The assembly remained intact with the keeper still on the link.

nodes.label: Work and Backup Rolls Removed for Outage
nodes.detail: Prior to the incident, work rolls and top/bottom backup rolls were removed from the stand.

nodes.label: Top Backup Roll Balance Left Isolated and Raised
nodes.detail: The top backup roll balance was left in an 'isolated' state, physically raised.

nodes.label: B Hydraulics Shut Off and Bled
nodes.detail: The B hydraulic system was shut off and bled prior to the incident.

nodes.label: Loss of Hydraulic Restraint on Carrier Beam Link
nodes.detail: Depressurizing the B hydraulics removed active support or restraint that was holding the carrier beam link/keeper assembly in place.

nodes.label: Raised Balance Altered Load Paths or Removed Support Point
nodes.detail: The 'isolated' and raised position of the top backup roll balance shifted load paths to rely solely on hydraulic pressure or mechanical retention that was compromised.

nodes.label: Absence of Secondary Mechanical Supports (Wedges/Stops)
nodes.detail: No physical stops, wedges, or secondary support devices were installed on the yoke/carrier beam assembly to prevent downward movement after hydraulics were bled.

nodes.label: Keeper Mechanism Not Rated for Gravity Loading Without Hydraulic Support
nodes.detail: The carrier beam keeper assembly is not designed or rated to retain the link under gravity-only loading conditions when hydraulic support is removed.

nodes.label: Failure in Shift Turnover Communication/Verification
nodes.detail: The previous shift did not explicitly communicate or verify the specific configuration (raised balance, bled hydraulics) to the incoming team via a formal sign-off.

nodes.label: Residual Pressure or Stored Energy in B Hydraulics System
nodes.detail: Trapped fluid in accumulators or lines created stored energy that actuated a mechanism holding the carrier beam, despite being 'bled'.

nodes.label: Missing Mechanical Assembly Drawing (EV-004)
nodes.detail: The specific mechanical design of how the carrier beam interacts with the yoke when hydraulics are bled and balances are raised is unknown due to missing documentation.

edges.rationale: Removal of rolls created the non-normal state where retention mechanisms were stressed or altered.
edges.counterfactual: If work rolls had remained installed during the outage preparation phase, would the carrier beam have fallen?
edges.competingExplanation: The fall was caused by a specific configuration change (raised balance + bled hydraulics) rather than just roll removal.
edges.evidenceGap: Need to verify if standard procedure requires secondary supports when rolls are removed.

edges.rationale: Raising the balance in an isolated state altered load paths or removed a critical support point for the yoke/carrier beam assembly.
edges.counterfactual: If the top backup roll balance had been lowered or not isolated before bleeding hydraulics, would the carrier beam have remained stable?
edges.competingExplanation: The fall was caused by loss of hydraulic pressure alone.
edges.evidenceGap: Need engineering drawings to confirm if raising the balance shifts load paths.

edges.rationale: Bleeding the B hydraulics removed active support or restraint that was holding the carrier beam link/keeper assembly in place.
edges.counterfactual: If B hydraulics had remained pressurized or a functional test confirmed zero energy before leaving the equipment, would the carrier beam have fallen?
edges.competingExplanation: The fall was caused by mechanical failure of the keeper due to wear/damage unrelated to hydraulic state.
edges.evidenceGap: Need P&ID/schematic to verify if B hydraulics actively restrain the link.

edges.rationale: The loss of hydraulic restraint directly precipitated the fall when gravity acted on the unsupported assembly.
edges.counterfactual: If a secondary mechanical stop was present, would loss of hydraulic restraint have caused the fall?
edges.competingExplanation: The keeper failed due to fatigue or corrosion independent of load path changes.
edges.evidenceGap: Need inspection history and component rating data.

edges.rationale: The raised balance created a new load path that exceeded the capacity of the keeper/link assembly under gravity.
edges.counterfactual: If the balance was not raised, would the load path have remained within design limits?
edges.competingExplanation: The fall occurred because no secondary support was used.
edges.evidenceGap: Need FEA or manual analysis of load paths for this specific configuration.

edges.rationale: The absence of physical stops or wedges allowed the assembly to move once hydraulic support was removed.
edges.counterfactual: If a mechanical stop had been installed, would the fall have occurred?
edges.competingExplanation: The keeper failed due to design limitation rather than lack of support.
edges.evidenceGap: Need work order and shift turnover logs confirming absence or removal of supports.

edges.rationale: The keeper mechanism was not designed to hold the load under gravity alone when hydraulics were bled.
edges.counterfactual: If the keeper was rated for gravity-only loading, would it have held?
edges.competingExplanation: The fall occurred because of a procedural gap (no secondary support) rather than component rating.
edges.evidenceGap: Need component specification sheet and design load ratings.

edges.rationale: Lack of formal communication or verification during shift turnover led to an unverified assumption that the equipment was safe.
edges.counterfactual: If a formal sign-off had occurred confirming the configuration, would the fall have been prevented?
edges.competingExplanation: The failure was mechanical and inevitable regardless of communication.
edges.evidenceGap: Need shift handover logs or witness statements.

edges.rationale: Residual pressure in the hydraulic system actuated a mechanism that released or compromised the carrier beam retention.
edges.counterfactual: If residual pressure had been verified and eliminated, would the fall have occurred?
edges.competingExplanation: The fall was caused by gravity acting on an unsupported load path.
edges.evidenceGap: Need hydraulic schematics and tryout logs.

edges.rationale: The absence of the mechanical assembly drawing prevents verification of whether hydraulic pressure was required for retention.
edges.counterfactual: If EV-004 were available, could we confirm if hydraulic pressure was a primary restraint?
edges.evidenceGap: Need to retrieve mechanical assembly drawing (EV-004).

edges.rationale: Without the drawing, we cannot confirm if raising the balance altered load paths.
edges.counterfactual: If EV-004 were available, could we confirm if raising the balance altered load paths?
edges.evidenceGap: Need to retrieve mechanical assembly drawing (EV-004).
